nodes.name: Tuesday 14:00 America/Los_Angeles
nodes.notes: Eight hours after the primary and five and a half after the fallback. If all three clocks worked, the published tree moved hours ago and this run sends nothing.

nodes.name: Read the published index
nodes.notes: CHANGE THE URL HERE if the published tree moves. It must be the index.json that `cfbpoll publish fixtures` writes, which carries seasons[].weeks[].published_at. onError is continueRegularOutput on purpose: a 404, a 500 or a timeout must reach the decision node as evidence, because an unreachable poll is exactly as alarming as an unpublished one and this switch exists to make silence audible.

nodes.name: Did this week publish?
nodes.notes: Emits ONE item when something is wrong and ZERO items when everything is fine, so the email node downstream simply does not run on a good Tuesday. No IF node, no filter syntax to get wrong across n8n versions.

nodes.name: Alert a human
nodes.notes: CHANGE toEmail TO john@thepoll.ai once that mailbox exists. Until then it goes to vyhlidal@gmail.com, which is the address that is actually read today. Needs an SMTP credential on the n8n instance; see docs/runbooks/sunday-automation.md.

parameters.subject: =[thepoll.ai] {{ $json.headline }}

meta.description: ADR 0002's dead-man's switch: if no published row exists for the current week by 14:00 PT Tuesday, alert. The recurring lesson of this project is that the dangerous failure is the silent one, so this makes silence itself the alarm - and note that it alarms on an UNREACHABLE index as loudly as on a stale one. Runbook: docs/runbooks/sunday-automation.md
